strengths: Compelling conceptual foundation: The paper presents an elegant and principled connection between online Bayesian continual learning (metaplasticity) and gated linear attention / state-space models, addressing both in-context catastrophic forgetting and catastrophic remembering.

Unifying theoretical framework: Table 1 and Section 2.3 provide clear insights into how prior models (Deltanets, Longhorn, MesaNet, Mamba2) can be viewed as specific instances or approximations within a common variational Bayesian objective.

Practical training strategy: Identifying that Mamba2 is an asymptotic special case of Palimpsa enables an efficient pre-training and fine-tuning workflow, successfully mitigating the training throughput overhead of dual-state updates.

Insightful synthetic analysis: The MQAR curriculum experiments and learning dynamic visualizations (Figure 2 and Figure 3) clearly validate the theoretical intuition, demonstrating that the effective window size $N_t$ and synaptic consolidation ratio dynamically adapt to prevent overwriting.

Solid empirical execution: Experiments across 170M and 760M models on FineWeb-Edu and standard commonsense reasoning benchmarks show consistent gains, particularly on long-context sensitive tasks such as LAMBADA.
weaknesses: Modest performance improvements on language benchmarks: On commonsense reasoning tasks at the 760M parameter scale, the average accuracy gains over strong non-metaplastic baselines are modest (e.g., 52.27% for Palimpsa-D fine-tuned vs. 51.82% for Palimpsa-D w/o Meta and 51.50% for Gated Deltanet), and Wikitext perplexity gains are marginal.

Full training vs. fine-tuning gap: At the 170M scale (Table 2), fully trained Palimpsa-D underperforms Palimpsa-D (w/o Meta) in average accuracy (43.45% vs. 43.91%), and only the fine-tuned checkpoint yields improvements. The paper would benefit from analyzing why training Palimpsa from scratch appears less effective or harder to optimize than fine-tuning.

Computational and inference overhead: Dual-state tracking incurs a noticeable hardware cost, leading to a $1.5\times\text{--}3\times$ slowdown during training and a $\approx 4\times$ slowdown in isolated attention inference throughput compared to Simple GLA (Figure 5).

Limited evaluation on long-context benchmarks: While the synthetic MQAR benchmark tests up to sequence length 1024, the paper lacks evaluations on long-context downstream benchmarks (e.g., LongBench, RULER, or needle-in-a-haystack tasks) where the benefits of mitigating catastrophic forgetting and remembering should be most pronounced.

strengths: Conceptual unification: The paper offers an elegant perspective that reframes in-context learning (ICL) in gated linear recurrence as an online continual learning problem with Bayesian metaplasticity, providing a unified variational free-energy formulation that relates Mamba2, Gated Deltanet, Longhorn, and MesaNet.

Insightful connection to Mamba2: Deriving Mamba2 as an asymptotic limiting case where forgetting dominates provides a solid theoretical motivation for the proposed 'pre-train fast, fine-tune metaplastic' training pipeline.

Implementation and scaling effort: Developing a chunk-wise associative scan Triton kernel for dual-state updates and evaluating models up to 760M parameters on 30B tokens goes beyond simple toy experiments often found in exploratory linear attention papers.

Diagnostic analysis: The learning dynamics analysis on the MQAR task (tracking the effective memory window N_t and synaptic metaplasticity ratio) nicely illustrates the hypothesized theoretical behavior.
weaknesses: Marginal empirical gains on language benchmarks: Across Commonsense Reasoning tasks at the 760M scale, the accuracy improvement over the non-metaplastic Gated Deltanet baseline is modest (52.27% vs. 51.50%, a gain of ~0.77%). Moreover, at the 170M scale, fully training Palimpsa-D from scratch actually underperforms the non-metaplastic ablation (43.45% vs. 43.91%), raising questions regarding optimization difficulty and robustness when training from scratch.

Severe computational and memory overhead: The requirement to track and parallelize dual states (Mt, It) introduces substantial register pressure and HBM traffic. As reported by the authors, training throughput is 1.5x to 3x slower than optimized GLA kernels, and generation throughput suffers an isolated ~4x slowdown. This significantly diminishes the core practical advantage of gated linear recurrence over standard softmax attention.

Theoretical heuristic in the diagonal approximation: Section A.5 notes that the diagonal precision matrix is obtained not by solving the variational free-energy under an explicit mean-field (diagonal) Gaussian constraint, but by first computing the coupled update and discarding off-diagonal terms post-hoc. A rigorous variational derivation under a diagonal covariance constraint would produce cross-terms that do not easily decouple, leaving a theoretical gap between the stated optimization problem and the implemented update rule.

Limited long-context evaluation: Given that the stability-plasticity dilemma and catastrophic remembering are particularly problematic over extended horizons, evaluating MQAR only up to sequence length 1024 is restrictive. Long-context benchmarks (e.g., 4k–32k sequence lengths or RULER / Needle-in-a-Haystack) are necessary to substantiate the claim that Palimpsa significantly expands memory capacity in long-sequence regimes.

strengths: Principled Bayesian formulation: The paper provides an elegant and mathematically rigorous derivation of gated linear attention updates through online variational free energy minimization. Grounding in-context learning in Bayesian continual learning and metaplasticity (MESU) provides a compelling conceptual bridge between neuroscience-inspired memory consolidation and modern sequence models.

Unifying theoretical framework: Table 1 and Section 2.3 establish a valuable unifying perspective showing how multiple recent architectures (Mamba-2, Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Longhorn, Mesanet) can be understood as specific variational posterior approximations and stability/plasticity parameterizations. In particular, demonstrating that Mamba-2 emerges as an asymptotic special case where forgetting dominates is an illuminating insight.

Practical training recipe: Leveraging the theoretical continuum between Mamba-2 and Palimpsa, the authors introduce a continuous reparameterization enabling efficient standard pre-training followed by short metaplastic fine-tuning. This effectively mitigates the computational cost of training dual-state models from scratch.

Solid empirical validation: The method is validated on both synthetic associative recall (MQAR) and real-world language modeling at academic scale (170M and 760M parameters on FineWeb-Edu). Metaplastic variants consistently improve associative recall at longer context lengths and achieve notable gains on memory-intensive benchmarks such as LAMBADA.

Transparency and implementation rigor: The authors provide detailed mathematical derivations in the appendix, discuss hardware-level implementation constraints (register pressure and memory traffic in Triton associative scan kernels), and transparently report inference and training throughput profiles.
weaknesses: Computational and memory overhead: Palimpsa requires maintaining and updating a dual-state recurrence (tracking both the precision matrix $I_t$ and the mean state $\mu_t$). As shown in the appendix, this results in a 1.5x–3x training throughput slowdown over Simple GLA and a ~4x inference slowdown for the isolated attention kernel. While the fine-tuning recipe helps during training, the runtime overhead at inference remains a practical limitation.

Absence of dedicated long-context LM benchmarks: The central motivation of the paper is mitigating catastrophic forgetting and extending effective context memory. While MQAR demonstrates this synthetically, language modeling evaluations are limited to standard zero-shot commonsense benchmarks and sequence lengths up to 2k. Evaluating on dedicated long-context retrieval/QA benchmarks (e.g., RULER, BABILong, or Needle-In-A-Haystack) would provide much stronger direct evidence of improved context retention in realistic settings.

Mixed results in full pre-training at 170M scale: In Table 2, fully trained Palimpsa-D underperforms its non-metaplastic ablation (43.45% vs 43.91% average accuracy), and only beats it when fine-tuned from the non-metaplastic checkpoint. Further analysis into optimization dynamics during early pre-training from scratch would clarify why cold-start metaplasticity underperforms fine-tuning.

strengths: Unifying theoretical framework: The paper provides a principled Bayesian formulation of in-context learning in gated linear recurrent attention and state-space models, clearly demonstrating how existing architectures (such as Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Longhorn, Mesanet, and Mamba2) emerge under specific approximations and prior/likelihood assumptions (Table 1).

Principled dual-state mechanism: Deriving metaplasticity (state-wise uncertainty/precision tracking via $I_t$) alongside state mean tracking ($\mu_t$) effectively addresses both catastrophic forgetting and catastrophic remembering in fixed-capacity recurrent memories.

Practical upgrade path: Demonstrating that Mamba2 is an asymptotic special case allows an efficient fine-tuning and 'surgical layer replacement' recipe on large models (e.g., 2.7B parameter scale), avoiding the high computational expense of training dual-state models entirely from scratch.

Comprehensive empirical validation: Experiments span synthetic recall (MQAR), academic-scale pre-training (170M and 760M on FineWeb-Edu), per-token NLL scaling across sequence length, and downstream long-context evaluations (LongBench, RULER) up to context lengths of 32k.
weaknesses: Computational and inference overhead: The dual-state update requires extra register pressure and memory tracking during chunked parallel associative scans, resulting in 1.5× to 3× slower training than baseline linear attention, and approximately 4× slower token generation during recurrent inference (Appendix A.13, Figure 7). This limits one of the main appeals of linear recurrent models (high generation throughput).

Optimization sensitivity when training from scratch: In the 170M evaluations (Table 2), fully training Palimpsa-D from scratch yields 43.45% average accuracy, underperforming both its fine-tuned counterpart (43.96%) and the non-metaplastic baseline (43.91%). The authors acknowledge that learning metaplasticity from random initialization is challenging, but further insight into why this happens or how to stabilize it is limited.

Mixed performance on long-context subtasks: While Palimpsa improves overall LongBench and 32k variable tracing, the RULER benchmark (Table 6) shows noticeable regressions on short-to-medium tracing (e.g., VT drops from 59.6 to 33.5 at 4k context) and aggregation tasks (CWE, FWE), which warrants deeper diagnostic analysis.
Minor presentation omission: In Section 'Code Availability' (page 10), the repository URL is left blank ('Our code is available at').

strengths: Principled Bayesian Formulation: The paper provides an elegant and mathematically sound formulation of in-context learning in gated linear models as variational free energy minimization with forgetting, bridging neuroscience-inspired metaplasticity and modern sequence models.

Theoretical Unification: Table 1 and Section 2.3 offer a compelling unification of existing gated linear models and SSMs (e.g., Longhorn, Deltanet, Gated Deltanet, Mesanet, and Mamba2) as specific posterior approximations or limiting regimes of a shared Bayesian objective.

Practical Conversion and Fine-tuning Strategy: Recognizing Mamba2 as an asymptotic special case of Palimpsa leads to an ingenious initialization and parameterization scheme, allowing existing pre-trained Mamba2 checkpoints to be surgically upgraded and fine-tuned into metaplastic models without costly pre-training from scratch.

Comprehensive Multi-Scale Empirical Evaluation: The method is validated across synthetic tasks (curriculum MQAR), pre-training and fine-tuning at 170M and 760M parameters, and a 2.7B surgical upgrade evaluated on long-context benchmarks (LongBench and RULER).
weaknesses: Computational and Memory Overhead: Maintaining a dual state (tracking both the mean state and the diagonal precision matrix) increases register pressure in chunked parallel scans. Training throughput is roughly 1.5x–3x slower than optimized GLA, and the recurrent inference kernel experiences a ~4x slowdown over Simple GLA.

Mixed Results on Specific Long-Context Sub-tasks: In the comprehensive RULER evaluation (Table 6), the fine-tuned metaplastic model substantially lags behind the Mamba2 baseline on aggregation tasks (CWE, FWE) across all sequence lengths and on single-needle retrieval tasks, indicating that adaptive precision may compromise tracking high-frequency or solitary features.

Training-from-Scratch Optimization Dynamics: At the 170M scale, fully trained Palimpsa-D slightly underperforms both the non-metaplastic baseline and its fine-tuned counterpart, indicating potential optimization difficulties or sensitivity to initialization when training precision dynamics from scratch.
Incomplete Code Availability Statement: The Code Availability section on page 10 ends abruptly ('Our code is available at ') without providing an anonymous repository link or reference.

strengths: Unifying theoretical perspective: The paper formulates in-context learning in recurrent attention as test-time online Bayesian linear regression with a sliding-window prior. Table 1 provides an illuminating conceptual framework connecting DeltaNet, Gated DeltaNet, MesaNet, and Mamba2 as specific variational approximations and limits of this objective.

Hardware-aware implementation: Deriving an associative scan formulation (Eq. 35) that allows parallelized chunk-wise computation in Triton demonstrates solid engineering and makes dual-state recurrent training feasible.

Resource-conscious surgical fine-tuning: The strategy of analyzing layer-wise memory windows ($N_t$) in pre-trained Mamba2 and selectively replacing only the weakest-forgetting layers offers a practical recipe for augmenting existing pre-trained checkpoints without requiring full pre-training from scratch.

Comprehensive experimental scope: Evaluations span synthetic associative recall (MQAR), academic pre-training across two scales (170M and 760M parameters on FineWeb-Edu), scaling up to a 2.7B checkpoint, long-context evaluations (LongBench, RULER), and hardware throughput benchmarks.
weaknesses: Substantial computational and memory overhead: Dual-state tracking ($M_t$ and $I_t$) introduces severe register pressure during chunk-wise scans. Appendix A.12 and A.13 report that Palimpsa is 1.5x to 3x slower during training compared to Simple GLA and incurs a ~4x throughput penalty during autoregressive inference (Figure 7). This significantly diminishes the core efficiency advantages of linear recurrent models over softmax attention.

Optimization difficulties when training from scratch: In Table 2, fully trained Palimpsa-D (170M) underperforms the non-metaplastic baseline (43.45% vs. 43.91% average accuracy, and higher WikiText/LAMBADA perplexity). The authors acknowledge that learning metaplasticity from random initialization is unstable, which severely restricts the practical utility of the model unless initialized from pre-trained non-metaplastic checkpoints.

Mixed and inconsistent long-context performance: While Palimpsa improves on certain long-horizon settings (e.g., 32k context on RULER Variable Tracing), it incurs severe performance drops on other tasks. On RULER (Table 6), Variable Tracing at shorter contexts collapses (dropping from 59.6 to 33.5 at 4k, and 49.7 to 24.9 at 8k), single-needle retrieval degrades, and frequent word extraction drops by up to 15 points. In LongBench, short-context tasks also experience an accuracy decline (18.9 to 16.1).

Modest downstream gains relative to the added complexity: On standard commonsense reasoning benchmarks at 170M and 760M scales, average accuracy improvements over baselines are marginal (around 0.6–0.8 points), which is within typical noise margins and hard to justify given the 4x inference slowdown.

Heuristic diagonal approximation: To make the update tractable, the full covariance matrix inverse is replaced by discarding off-diagonal terms after derivation (Appendix A.5). As noted by the authors, this is an ad-hoc simplification rather than a principled mean-field derivation, weakening the exact Bayesian guarantees of the formulation.
